The effect of two groups per study, with its naive and exact standard errors

Source: R/se_imputed_df.R
se_imputed_diff.Rd

For a data set with two groups side by side (the columns of one group carry one suffix, those of the other group another), runs se_imputed_df on each group and appends the effect of the study, group 1 against group 2, with its standard error under the naive and under the exact standard errors: the difference of means (measure = "MD", the default) or the log variability ratio (measure = "lnVR"), in the column names that metafor::rma() takes as they are, yi and sei. pool_imputed pools the result in one call.

Usage

se_imputed_diff(
  data,
  suffixes = c(".g1", ".g2"),
  ...,
  measure = c("MD", "lnVR"),
  version = c("blue", "wan_luo_shi"),
  prefer = c("sample", "imputed"),
  type = 7
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per study.

suffixes

The two suffixes of the groups' columns, group 1 first. The default is the layout of the data sets shipped with the metamedian package, ".g1" and ".g2".

...

The column-name arguments of se_imputed_df (n, min, q1, med, q3, max, mean, sd), passed to both groups.

measure

The effect per study: "MD" (default), the difference of the two means, group 1 minus group 2; or "lnVR", the log variability ratio of Nakagawa et al. (2015), the log of the SD of group 1 over the SD of group 2. See Details.

version

"blue" (default) or "wan_luo_shi", as in se_imputed.

prefer

What to use for a row that has both a summary and a sample mean and SD: "sample" (default), the sample statistics, or "imputed".

type

The definition of the reported sample quantiles, 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default. One value for every row.

Value

data with the output columns of se_imputed_df for each group (each with its suffix) and three more: yi, the effect; sei_naive, its standard error from the naive standard errors; and sei, its standard error from the exact ones. The result carries the attribute "measure", which pool_imputed reads for its heading. A row that se_imputed_df() could not use in either group has NA in the three columns.

Details

The two groups are independent samples, so the variances add.

Under "MD", \(y_i = \hat\mu_{i1} - \hat\mu_{i2}\), sei_naive \(= (\mathrm{se\_naive}_{i1}^2 + \mathrm{se\_naive}_{i2}^2)^{1/2}\) and sei \(= (\mathrm{se\_mu}_{i1}^2 + \mathrm{se\_mu}_{i2}^2)^{1/2}\).

Under "lnVR", \(y_i = \log(\hat\sigma_{i1}/\hat\sigma_{i2})\), and the variance of \(y_i\) is approximated by the sum of one term per group, to first order in each group's SD (the delta method, \(\mathrm{Var}(\log X) \approx \mathrm{Var}(X)/(\mathrm{E}X)^2\)). The naive variance gives every group the large-sample term of the log of a sample SD of \(n\) normal observations, \(1/\{2(n - 1)\}\), so sei_naive \(= \{1/(2(n_{i1} - 1)) + 1/(2(n_{i2} - 1))\}^{1/2}\). The exact variance keeps that term for a group that gives its sample SD and uses \(C^2_\sigma(n)\), the exact variance of the imputed SD in units of \(\sigma^2\), for a group whose SD is imputed (from the quartiles, the extremes, or the range alone), which the group's columns carry as (se_sigma / sigma_hat)^2; sei is the square root of the sum of the two terms. These are the two variances of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026): exact in the factor \(C_\sigma(n)\), first-order in the log, so neither is the finite-sample variance of the log ratio, and the intervals of pool_imputed are normal approximations. The small-sample bias correction of Nakagawa et al. (2015), which metafor::escalc(measure = "VR") adds to \(y_i\), is not applied, as in Wu, Shi and Tong (2026). Both analyses use the plain log ratio.

References

Nakagawa S, Poulin R, Mengersen K, Reinhold K, Engqvist L, Lagisz M, Senior AM (2015). Meta-analysis of variation: ecological and evolutionary applications and beyond. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 6(2), 143-152.

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

See also

se_imputed_df, se_imputed, pool_imputed.

Examples

two <- data.frame(n.g1 = c(25, 30), q1.g1 = c(10, 11), med.g1 = c(12, 13), q3.g1 = c(15, 16),
                  n.g2 = c(29, 40), q1.g2 = c(8, 9), med.g2 = c(10, 11), q3.g2 = c(13, 14))
d <- se_imputed_diff(two)
d[, c("yi", "sei_naive", "sei")]
#>         yi sei_naive       sei
#> 1 2.001110 1.0672925 1.1478665
#> 2 2.002044 0.9333307 0.9977329
pool_imputed(d)                                    # the pooled difference, both SEs
#> Pooled difference of means (group 1 minus group 2), common-effect model (EE), 2 studies
#>          estimate     se  ci.lb ci.ub     pval         Q I2
#> naive SE    2.002 0.7026 0.6246 3.379 0.004386 4.337e-07  0
#> exact SE    2.002 0.7530 0.5257 3.478 0.007858 3.769e-07  0
#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values from the normal distribution. Q has 1 degrees of freedom, and I2 is in percent.
#> The weights in percent are $weights. Every field with str() or unclass().
v <- se_imputed_diff(two, measure = "lnVR")       # the log ratio of the SDs
v[, c("yi", "sei_naive", "sei")]
#>            yi sei_naive       sei
#> 1 0.008045533 0.1966989 0.3233439
#> 2 0.011700746 0.1733837 0.2791642
# columns named otherwise, two groups with the suffixes "_t" and "_c"
spread <- data.frame(N_t = 25, Min_t = 3, Median_t = 12, Max_t = 30,
                     N_c = 29, Min_c = 2, Median_c = 10, Max_c = 25)
se_imputed_diff(spread, suffixes = c("_t", "_c"), n = "N", min = "Min",
                med = "Median", max = "Max")[, c("yi", "sei_naive", "sei")]
#>         yi sei_naive      sei
#> 1 2.337257  1.730794 1.963484
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
metafor::rma(yi, sei = sei, data = d)          # the pooled difference with the exact SEs
metafor::rma(yi, sei = sei_naive, data = d)    # the same with the naive SEs, for comparison
} # }
